chunks: Hammad, from Hareez, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
'Indeed the salat was always a timed ordinance upon the believers'

key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: Salat — the prescribed Islamic prayer, one of the pillars of faith
key_terms.كِتَاباً مَوْقُوتاً: A timed ordinance/decree — the Quranic phrase from 4:103 interpreted by the Imam as signifying a binding obligation
key_terms.مَوْجُوباً: Wajib/obligatory — the jurisprudential term indicating a binding religious duty

ai.seo_question: What does 'kitaban mawqutan' mean in Quran 4:103 according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In this narration, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) provides an authoritative interpretation of Quran 4:103, clarifying that the word 'mawqut' (timed) in the verse means that salat is a firm obligation (wajib) prescribed at fixed times. This commentary, transmitted through the highly reliable chain of Zurara from the Imam, establishes the jurisprudential ruling that prayer is not merely encouraged but is mandatory. The original audience, the early Shia community, would have understood this as grounding their prayer obligations in explicit Quranic authority as interpreted by their Imam.
